findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with nil TopicUser for users who have no topic record
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is not guarded. A logged-in user who has never interacted with the topic (e.g. a user reached by a notification email for a topic they only got via mention or digest, or whose record was never created) has no TopicUser row, so `tu` is nil and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 from the unsubscribe link. Use `TopicUser.change` or find-or-create the record.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET that toggles, so mail scanners can change settings and a second click re-subscribes
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes notification level on a GET request, and the action toggles: if the level is above regular it is set to regular, otherwise to muted. Email link scanners and prefetchers that fetch URLs will silently unsubscribe users. A user who clicks the link twice gets re-subscribed, because the second request flips the state back. Unsubscribe should set an explicit target state (muted) idempotently, ideally via POST with a token.

findings.title: unsubscribe writes via save! and bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: The action sets `notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. It does not set `notifications_reason_id` or `notifications_changed_at`, which `TopicUser.change` sets, and it does not publish the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message, so open clients for the user won't update. The read-then-write sequence also loses updates under concurrent requests.

findings.title: Ember template name does not match the route, so the unsubscribe page template is never rendered
findings.body: The route is declared as top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`. Ember resolves its template as `topic-unsubscribe`, but the file added is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which resolves to `topic/unsubscribe`. The controller and view are also named `topic-unsubscribe`. The page will render with no template, so the feature's UI does not appear.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The property is spelled `stopNotificiationsText` here and in the template. It works only because both sides use the same typo. It should be corrected before it spreads to plugins or other code.

findings.title: track_visit! uses the topic argument as user_id when a User is not passed
findings.body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to the topic argument instead of the user argument. When a plain user id is passed, the query updates or creates rows for the wrong user, using the topic id as the user id. The line was touched by this PR but the bug was left in place.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link i18n now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link email
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` renders it whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is set, and it only supplies `unsubscribe_url` here. Any other caller (including plugins) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` will now raise an interpolation error when building the email, both in the HTML part and the text body. Either make the key optional or fall back to a safe value.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe sentence appears for every email, not only topic notifications
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` text now always includes the 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' line. That is correct for the notification path but misleading for any other email that uses this key with a generic or non-topic context. The message should be scoped to the topic emails.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url builds on url, which includes the post number and slug
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url` is `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` and `url` takes no post number here, so this is fine. However it depends on `slug`, which is lazily computed and may be empty for a topic with a blank title. The result is then `/t//id/unsubscribe`, and the controller's slug check redirects to a different URL on each call. Consider building it from `relative_url` or `id` only.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or for the per-topic unsubscribe email text
findings.body: The spec change only adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing builder test. Nothing tests the controller's toggle logic, the missing-TopicUser case, the 301 redirect on slug mismatch, or that the email body includes the topic unsubscribe link. The crash path above would have been caught by a request spec for a user without a TopicUser row.

findings.title: Summary route constraints silently changed while adding unsubscribe routes
findings.body: The diff reorders the moderator-liked and summary routes and drops `post_number: /\d+/` from the summary constraints. These are unrelated to unsubscribe and are not explained in the PR, which increases the risk of unintended routing changes. Keep this PR to the unsubscribe routes.

findings.title: Unrelated refactor of topic-from-params route included in an unsubscribe feature PR
findings.body: The file is rewritten from `var` to `const`, the `self` variable is moved, and blank lines are changed. None of this supports the unsubscribe feature. It increases review surface and merge-conflict risk. Split it into a separate change.
